title: Working after losing a baby | NHS inform
text:
Working after losing a baby
There’s no right answer as to when you should go back to work. But, it’s important to give yourself time to recover physically and emotionally.
You may wish to return to work as soon as possible after a loss. But, you may also feel that you need more time away from work.
Your partner, if you have one, may also need to take some time away from work to recover themselves, or to care for you.
Paid leave
There’s no legal requirement for employers to provide specific pregnancy loss leave or pay.
Some workplaces do have a specific pregnancy loss policy. This will set out the support they can offer you. For information on what may be available to you, speak to your employer.
Sickness absence
If you need time off work because of a loss, this should be treated as pregnancy related sickness. This covers time off you need to take during and after losing a baby.
You can self-certify for 7 calendar days. This means you can take 7 days in a row off of work without providing evidence of your illness to your employer. These 7 days includes weekends, even if you don’t normally work weekends.
After 7 days, you’ll need to provide your employer with a fit note. This proves that your time off is pregnancy-related sickness.
Read more about getting a fit note
Maternity Action
have more information about your rights to time off and pay.
Other types of leave
You and your partner may be able to ask your employer for compassionate leave.
You may be able to agree a period of leave if you need time beyond sickness absence. You’ll need to discuss this with your employer.
Your rights
The
Equality Act 2010
protects you from discrimination based on pregnancy or pregnancy-related sickness. This includes a period of 2 weeks after losing a baby. If you need to take pregnancy-related sick leave, you’re protected from discrimination.
Support if you’re returning to work
Specialist charities and organisations provide information about returning to work after miscarriage. They may also offer advice if you think your workplace has mistreated you after losing a baby.
Maternity Action
aims to protect the rights of workers who’ve experienced pregnancy loss. They have advice about your rights to time off and pay after losing a baby.
Miscarriage Association
offers support and information to anyone affected by miscarriage. This is for employees, employers, managers, HR and colleagues.
SANDS
offers support in Scotland and information for anyone affected by the death of a baby. This includes
advice about returning to work after your loss
.
Tommy’s
provides information and support after pregnancy loss. It offers tailored advice about
going back to work after losing a baby
.
